cards.title: A quarter of dead trunks flicker shadowless (#47)
cards.detail: VARY has no real floor — (dh >> 13) % span is a signed shift on an unsigned hash, so 48.8% of pieces get a negative term. Do NOT fix by flipping the shift: that re-rolls the size of half the scenery on every island that already exists. Fix by shadowing by KIND, or correct the test.
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug by the SECOND route — the test was corrected and the render was deliberately left alone. The title is also wrong and worth correcting for anyone searching: they do not FLICKER. Size is a pure function of the hash, so a given trunk is the same size every time the island loads; 'flicker' was never observed, only inferred. The card's numbers all held when measured over 15,129 pieces (48.8% negative terms, dead trunks 0.252-0.868 tall, 24.5% shadowless), but the product turned out to be RIGHT: the smallest dead trunk is shorter than the reed and narrower than the tuft that the shadow rule already excludes on purpose, so excluding it is consistent rather than a bug. The actual defect was shadow.test.ts:306 asserting a floor that does not exist. `varyMin` now sits beside `varyMax` and the four .min-as-floor assertions moved onto it. Also settled: VARY is ONE definition, not five copies — the other four files the card named carry nothing. LEFT FOR JOE, blocking nothing: whether a 0.25-unit dead trunk with no blob shadow looks right to him. Shadow-by-kind would add blobs to islands that already exist, so it needs his eye first.

cards.title: Batch the blob shadows before the 40-tile island (#47b)
cards.detail: createBlobShadow makes fresh geometry AND material per blob; +1 draw call each, ~70 extra at 40 tiles. Must exclude pets, whose castShadow mutates opacity per frame. Natural home: beside the Phase 5 lighting rework.
cards.note: SURVEYED 1 Aug, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — the card's 'natural home is Phase 5' is right and the reason is now measured rather than assumed. Findings so the Phase 5 run starts ahead: (1) SHARING THE MATERIAL DOES NOT DO WHAT THE CARD WANTS. In three.js a draw call is per MESH, so a shared material saves memory and state changes but leaves the ~70 draw calls exactly where they are. Only merging or instancing removes them. Anyone picking this up should not report a shared material as a fix. (2) THE CHEAP HALF THAT IS REAL: every blob builds its own CircleGeometry(radius, 20) purely because the radius differs. A unit CircleGeometry(1, 20) plus a per-mesh scale renders identically and collapses ~70 geometries to one. Safe, testable, and worth doing on its own — but it is an allocation win, not a draw-call win. (3) WHO MAY BE BATCHED: props create their blob once and never touch it again (props.ts:697, via a static holder), so they are mergeable. Pets are NOT — pets.ts:1079 calls castShadow every frame, which mutates opacity and scale, so a shared material would make every pet's shadow fade and swell together. Fred and the egg sit with the pets on the safe side: the egg's is shaped once and left, per the comment at juice.ts:128. (4) THE ACTUAL OBSTACLE, which is why this belongs beside the lighting rework and not before it: prop blobs are parented under each prop's own holder, and props are placed INCREMENTALLY as she builds tiles. A merged island-space mesh therefore needs rebuilding whenever a tile is added or a prop is removed, which is a lifecycle question about the prop field rather than a shadow question. Solve it with the lighting, or not at all.

cards.title: Prop glTFs 404 on a texture that is never used (#45)
cards.detail: props/*.gltf reference hexagons_medieval.png but the folder ships only the _Summer variant. Harmless, but it has cost two agents time. A clean console is a debugging tool. Cheapest fix is the loading manager.
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug, and the card's instinct was right — a LoadingManager rewrites that one URL to a 1x1 PNG data URI. All 37 prop glTFs asked for it; forest and tiles were checked and are clean, so props was the only source of red. THE THING WORTH KNOWING, because the obvious fix is wrong: deleting the image from the 37 files removes the baseColorTexture declaration, and that declaration is what makes GLTFLoader compile the map define into the material's shader. Nothing in props.ts calls needsUpdate after assigning .map, so stripping it would render EVERY PROP UNTEXTURED. The broken reference is load-bearing, which is plausibly why two agents noticed it and neither touched it. Pointing it at the _Summer file that does exist would also work but makes GLTFLoader fetch and decode a full atlas 37 times to build textures thrown away on the next line. Tests guard the NARROW side rather than the hit: a URL modifier sits in front of every prop fetch, and the real risk is swallowing a texture that exists — tiles/hexagons_medieval.png is a real and different file, and an endsWith on the bare filename would have eaten it. One test also asserts the props folder still lacks the file, so if anyone ever ships it this fix is flagged as dead weight rather than left to confuse. Gates all five green; the clean console follows from there being no network fetch at all, and was not separately eyeballed in a browser.

STATUS 29 Jul: OPEN, AND THE BRIEF HAS NOW LANDED - docs/pet-island-species-roster.md, 142 lines, ratified rather than draft. It arrived mid-way through the backlog reconciliation (Joe's commit 8189a5e), so this card was OPEN AND UNSPECIFIED for most of the day and is not any more. BUILD TO THE ROSTER, NOT TO A SUMMARY OF IT, including not to this card - read it in full first. His one-sentence acceptance test still governs and does not depend on the roster: 'i cannot run out of animal rewards' - the supply must not be exhaustible by a child who keeps playing. WHAT THE ROSTER SETTLES, in brief and only as a pointer: ~296 new builds across 20 collections on top of the live base 24, explicitly NOT a build order - collections ship ONE AT A TIME on the existing 85% unlock cadence, so do not attempt the roster in one run and do not let the scale tempt anyone into generating species in bulk without review. KITS BEFORE SPECIES is the architecture and the whole leverage: six kits (quadruped, songbird, raptor, swim, minibeast, bespoke), built once, after which a species is DATA - proportions, palette, two or three detail parts. THE LIVE 24 ARE FROZEN: never rebuilt, never restyled, though their geometry is fair game as a starting point. Roster 6 carries Joe's OWN open questions (ship order, whether Prehistoric ships at all, IUCN wording) - those are his, to be raised in the workbench when they block, and NOT to be settled with Fable. WHAT IS MEASURED TODAY, so the brief can be read against it rather than re-derived. THE SUPPLY IS FINITE AND ITS SIZE IS 600: pets.ts:20-26 SPECIES is a fixed 24-entry list of Kenney GLB basenames, sets.ts:105-145 SETS is 25 (1 natural + 12 solid + 12 stripy; the spotted twelve were dropped because the texture cannot carry dots, and the legendary ten are PB-029), and sets.ts:160 totalVariants = 25 x 24 = 600. So it is 600, not the brief's ~1,000. Stale comment to fix while you are there: main.ts:420-422 and :1185 still say '19 candidates' and 'one time in 19' against a 24-entry SPECIES. TWO EXPENSIVE FACTS FROM HANDOFF 6 THAT CONSTRAIN ANY DESIGN: a set is ONE RECOLOURED ATLAS, not a per-variant texture, because every species shares a single material (atlas.ts:111-166, cache key setId/speciesId); and set textures are CACHED AND DETACHED, NEVER DISPOSED, because disposing one breaks every pet of that set including ones she already owns (brief 19). THE NAMING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED BY THE ROSTER, AND THE ANSWER CARRIES A BRIEF-19 TRAP - this is the first thing to get right, ahead of any species work. Roster 3 replaces today's behaviour: the given name becomes the alien-word generator SEEDED DETERMINISTICALLY FROM species + set, so every child's blue-set hedgehog is the same Bimo forever, plus a real fixed species name as 'playground currency'. Names are generated once, audited, and frozen AS DATA - never regenerated, or the shared bond breaks. THE TRAP: PET NAMES TODAY ARE PROCEDURALLY GENERATED PER HATCH FROM UNSEEDED Math.random - petName(defaultRng) at main.ts:1167, defaultRng = Math.random at core/rng.ts:5 - and the name never sees the species or the set, so two children get different names for the same lion. It IS persisted once drawn (flow.ts:311-312 bakes it into the Pet record, save.ts:171/226 round-trips it), so nothing is lost on reload. But sets.ts:13-16 and :162-168 already DECLARE the opposite intent - 'Names are fixed per variant and graded by set (brief 5, voice.md 2)', with variantKey documented as 'Used for the name table' - and that name table does not exist anywhere in the code. Whether the brief keeps procedural naming or replaces it with the fixed per-variant table sets.ts already assumes is a genuine open question, so JUNO ALREADY OWNS PETS WHOSE NAMES WERE DRAWN RANDOMLY, and a naive switch to deterministic naming RENAMES THE CREATURES SHE HAS ALREADY HATCHED. That is a brief 19 violation - nothing she owns is ever lost, and a pet's name is the most personal thing she owns. JOE HAS SINCE ANSWERED THIS AND HIS ANSWER IS SIMPLER THAN A MIGRATION LAYER (c54e286, 29 Jul): 'i will give you juno's already achieved animal's names as her latest save game later, you can swap the first hard code out after.' So HER EXISTING PETS' NAMES BECOME THE CANONICAL DETERMINISTIC NAMES for those species+set pairs - pinned as data in the frozen name table, not migrated around. Nothing of hers changes, and the table is right for every other child too, because the table IS the source of truth. What follows for the build: the name table must be DATA WITH PINNABLE ENTRIES FROM DAY ONE, so a supplied name overrides a generated one for a given species+set - that is the seam her save plugs into; a TEMPORARY HARDCODE IS EXPLICITLY SANCTIONED until her save arrives ('swap the first hard code out after'), and it must be marked unmistakably as >>> PROVISIONAL with the exact lines named in the handoff; DO NOT BUILD A GENERAL RENAME-MIGRATION MECHANISM - it is not needed and would be a large risky thing built for a case that will not occur; still write the 19 test (hatch under the old scheme, move to the new, assert the old pet is untouched), and because the id EMBEDS the name (flow.ts:311-312, id 'pet'+n+'-'+name) check what an id migration would touch before assuming either path is safe. HER SAVE HAS NOT ARRIVED YET: do not invent her pets' names to fill the table, exactly as you must not invent species. Leave the pins empty and obvious. Note also that sets.ts:13-16 and :162-168 already ANTICIPATED this - 'Names are fixed per variant and graded by set (brief 5, voice.md 2)', with variantKey documented as 'Used for the name table' - so the roster is ratifying an intent the code has carried unimplemented all along. THE AUDIT IS JOE'S MANUAL WORK AND IT IS LARGE: every generated name needs checking for pronunciation and for real-word or rude-word collisions, and name audio is baked in Olivia's voice. The audit surface is therefore a FIRST-CLASS DELIVERABLE, not a byproduct. HIS REVIEW WILL LIKELY HAPPEN OUTSIDE THE DRUMBEAT, in a session of his own ('lots of manual review work that i may do in a separate session'), so the review surface must be resumable, must not need a manager running, and must not be a wall of prose - it belongs in the workbench in reviewable units, the way joe/noun-candidates.json and joe/pairs-audit.json already work (JT-004 and JT-005 are the pattern to read before designing it). cards.title: A7 regression: the reading page mix quietly doubled the find pages
cards.detail: Found while surveying A3's deal path, not yet fixed. main.ts passes state.readProgress to dealReading as the PAGE INDEX, and deal.ts:69 asks pageKind(page), which is mix[page % 4] over ['find','build','build','build']. Since A7 readProgress counts UNITS and advances by pay.item = 2 per page, so the index goes 0,2,4,6 and the mix reads find,build,find,build - one find page in two, where the data says one in four. Demonstrated: pre-A7 'find build build build find build' vs today 'find build find build find build'. This is exactly the trap A7's own field note names ('anything asserting pacing should ask in items, or it is asserting the denomination instead'); the month-walk pinned COSTS in items and the page mix was never asked. Fix is at the deal path, not in balance.json - the index wants converting from units to items (readProgress / itemPay(), exact because a reading page pays exactly one item) - and it needs a test that pins the mix a child actually SEES across an egg, since the existing balance.test.ts pins pageKind(0..3) directly and cannot see this. Note before changing it: alternating find/build may well be the nicer mix. The bug is that nobody chose it. CLOSED 28 Jul with A3. Joe ruled it (JT-010(2)): 'reading mix should be 3 build, 1 find. period.' The data was right all along; balance.pagesRead() converts units to pages at the deal path, and the new tests in balance.test.ts walk readProgress the way the game moves it instead of asking pageKind(0..3) directly - which is why the old suite could not see it.

cards.title: A page she abandons is re-measured when she re-does it
cards.detail: A consequence of JT-009(c), recorded rather than fixed, because fixing it costs more than it does. She finds 11 of 12 words, taps X, and comes back to the same page whole - so those 11 words are answered TWICE and emitted twice, and the second pass is easier by construction because she has just done them. Abandonment therefore nudges accuracy UP a little. Why it is small: the latency ring is 30 deep and the EWMA alpha is .15, so a handful of repeats move nothing you can see, and it needs a child who actually leaves pages mid-way to appear at all. Why it is not fixed: de-duplicating attempts per card would mean the tally knowing what a CARD is - which store it came from, whether it is the same one - and attempts.ts was deliberately split out of the overlay to keep it arithmetic over an event order rather than a thing that knows about ReadPick. The honest cheap alternative if it ever matters is to mark the repeat rather than drop it: challengeFailed already sets readHeld, so the overlay knows on the way back IN that this page is a re-visit, and one bit on AttemptEvent would let A6 decide. Trigger: if the grown-ups report ever reads flattering for a child who leaves a lot, look here first. STILL OPEN AND STILL RIGHT after Run B - attempts.ts:39-53 still carries only kind/index/correct/latency with no repeat bit, and EWMA_ALPHA is still .15 (harness.ts:182). But the 'moves nothing you can see' estimate was made BEFORE Run B, and Run B added three new consumers of the same attempt stream: the probe ring, the mercy counter and the weakness lean (harness.ts:1036-1053, 1086). A duplicated attempt now also feeds the mercy trigger, which fires on a run of three - a much shorter window than a 30-deep ring - so the effect is no longer purely diluted. Re-estimate the size before deciding it is still too small to fix.

cards.title: The governors say 'invitation' and behave like a refusal
cards.progress: SPLIT IN TWO by manager run 1, because Joe reported it live: the deployed build was 'erroneously forcing tile building' with Juno frustrated by it. cards.detail: Raised by Joe, 28 July, correcting a claim made in session: "there is currently a hard bound. if there are not enough tiles for the number of animals, it says 'they need more homes' and wont let you do an egg. same probably applies the other way round." He is right, and it applies both ways. THE GAP between the doctrine and the behaviour: governors.ts:8-14 states "They are INVITATIONS, never lockouts. Nothing greys out; Fred asks for the other thing instead, and the child may ignore him." The first half is true and the second is not. interactions.ts:82-89 (egg) and :140-141 (socket) call invite() and return the flow UNCHANGED - the round never opens. So nothing greys out, the tap can be repeated forever and nothing already earned is taken away, but she cannot actually do the thing she asked for. 'The child may ignore him' is precisely what she cannot do. That is a lockout with a warm line on it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: brief 19 is the rule the whole project bends to - invitations never lockouts, nothing expires, nothing is taken back - and a doctrine comment that misdescribes its own code is how a future change gets justified by a rule it does not actually follow. PB-039 does NOT fix this; it moves WHEN the stop fires (the maths-push end from ~1.2 tiles per animal out to 3 animals per 2 tiles, so she meets it far less often) and leaves the mechanism alone. THREE WAYS TO CLOSE IT, Joe's call. (a) MAKE THE CODE MATCH THE DOCTRINE: Fred asks, and if she taps again the round opens anyway - the ask becomes real and she may override it. Softest, and the truest to brief 19. (b) MAKE THE DOCTRINE MATCH THE CODE: keep the hard stop, rewrite the comment to say so honestly - a bound the child cannot cross is a legitimate design, it is just not an invitation. (c) SPLIT THEM: the ratio corridor is a genuine stop, the break-watch stays an invitation, and the doctrine distinguishes the two kinds. Nothing should be built here until he picks one, because (a) and (b) are opposite answers to the same sentence. ANSWERED by Joe, 28 July (JT-012), and it is none of the three cleanly - it is (a) with a fourth thing behind it: "tough one. it should start with invitation first, the let the user run with whatever they want to do up to a point otherwise we risk breaking the balance of the island. we then make the reward really really tough to reach the reward if it pushes imbalance further if its too far out of balance. with an announcement. match this to PB-042 when we pick it up. target ratio i think should be 1 animal per 2 tiles, with a buffer to 2:3 either way, then it starts to become increasingly tougher to get either." So the stop is replaced by a PRICE. Invitation first and she may override it; past the buffer the thing she is over-buying gets progressively dearer rather than refused, announced so it is never a silent tax. Nothing is ever taken away, which keeps brief 19, and the island cannot be broken, which is what the hard stop was protecting. BUILD IS EXPLICITLY HELD by Joe ("hold build until we pick up PBI#42") - this card is where it gets picked up. THREE THINGS THE BUILD WILL NEED SETTLING FIRST, all numeric. (1) His target here is ONE ANIMAL PER TWO TILES - 2.0 tiles per animal - which is NOT what the code holds: balance.json's tilesPerPet is 1.5, three tiles per two animals, his own earlier ruling of 28 July. PB-039 shipped against 1.5. Whether 2.0 supersedes 1.5 or describes the far end of the new buffer is the first question. (2) 'a buffer to 2:3 either way' needs pinning as two ratios; 2:3 either side of a 1:2 target is not symmetric in tiles-per-pet and the two walls have to be written out as numbers before anything is coded. (3) The escalation curve: how much dearer, over what distance, and does it cap. Note the cost curves are the WRONG place to look for the equilibrium itself - 17ad266 established that egg and tile are the same curve to within rounding - but a deliberate divergence between them is precisely the mechanism this ruling asks for, which is the first time that has been true.

cards.title: The reading progression curriculum
cards.detail: RAISED BY JOE HIMSELF, 29 Jul, and it arrived on the wrong card - it is the note he closed ruling JT-025 with, so it would have been lost inside a closed ruling if it did not become a card. His words, in full: 'we need to catch up here with the reading progression curriculum. 1. adding nouns 2. finding word challenge with only similar words. 3. 5-letter longer non-noun words, etc etc.' WHY IT EXISTS: B2 shipped a honeymoon that makes MATHS cheaper only, while the offer she hears promises 'eggs and tiles faster'. Joe was asked whether to reword the promise and answered JT-024 with 'see answer to JT-025' - so he did NOT reverse B2 and nothing is to be reverted; his fix is to build the reading side until the promise becomes true. THIS IS A SURVEY-THEN-ASK CARD, NOT A BUILD-TO-SPEC ONE. His three rungs are a sketch and his own 'etc etc' says so. Reading already has real machinery (src/challenges/wordFind, the noun lists in joe/) and the maths ladder PB-030 is the worked precedent, so the job is to map what exists against his three rungs and hand him the questions the sketch leaves open. WHAT PB-030 PROVED IS GENERAL AND SHOULD BE COPIED: selection lives in the island layer and never in src/core/, because golden.json pins per-level generator behaviour and parity.mjs drives v0's own level switch, so the two regression gates constrain a ladder from opposite directions; nothing demotes, ever, and the cheapest way to honour that is to make regression EMERGENT from the estimate rather than a stored flag; one offer a session, and a decline costs nothing but a cooldown; a capability tick is a parent's statement and must always outrank an estimate; probes go into their own ring. WHAT IS SPECIFIC TO MATHS AND MUST NOT BE COPIED BLINDLY: (a) the one-pool, share-follows-tick-count model exists because maths has exactly TWO peer paths, whereas reading's build/find split is already governed by a FIXED 3-build-1-find mix Joe ruled in JT-010(2) - so a weakness lean in reading would collide with that ruling the same way B3's lean collided with JT-010(1). Expect that conflict and raise it early. (b) pagesRead derives the reading page by dividing progress by the pay rate, so reading's difficulty and reading's economy are coupled in a way maths's are not; B2 already hit this. (c) the promotion constants (ewma >= .85, >= 20 attempts, >= 2 distinct days) are calibrated to SHORT maths items and must be re-derived, not inherited, for items that take much longer. AND THE LESSON THAT SAVED B3: check each spec clause against joe/tasks.json before building it. Run A's spec paragraphs are dense and were written before Joe's rulings existed.

cards.title: asset loading optimisation
cards.detail: investigation/discussion first on how to cleverly serve the game to balance memory and runtime load lag, given all the audio, flora and fauna.
cards.note: THE INVESTIGATION IS DONE, 1 Aug — docs/asset-loading-survey.md, measured against a real build. NOTHING WAS BUILT, deliberately: the card says 'investigation/discussion first' and the five decisions are Joe's, raised as JT-039. The card stays OPEN because the discussion has not happened. WHAT THE SURVEY FOUND. (1) The scale problem is already solved and the KITS solved it, not anything to do with loading: a Kenney GLB is ~141 KB per species so 296 would be ~41.7 MB, while a parts-bank definition is ~9.9 KB of source so 296 are ~2.9 MB — fourteenfold, and it gzips far better again. (2) The real issue is EAGER PARSING, not size: it all compiles into ONE JS chunk, 297 KB gzipped today, so every species she has never unlocked is parsed at boot while JT-027 caps her at four open collections. The splitting seam already exists and is the unit she unlocks. (3) THE CARD'S PREMISE IS PARTLY STALE — there is NO AUDIO AT ALL. Not one sound file ships; speech is Azure at runtime and the 43 phonemes are still JT-006. Audio is a future weight whose shape is entirely open, which is why it is worth ruling on now. (4) NOT ASKED ABOUT BUT PROBABLY THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE: the game does not work offline. vite.island.config.ts:69 precaches only js/css/html/woff2 with no runtimeCaching — 8 precache entries, not one 3D model. On a tablet with no connection it boots to a shell and cannot load a single animal, tile, tree or mountain. Recorded as a measurement rather than filed as a card, because whether it is a defect depends on Joe's answer to question 3. DO NOT BUILD A CACHING OR SPLITTING STRATEGY until that one is answered — offline support and lazy-loading pull in opposite directions and building either first makes the other dearer.

cards.title: An abandoned tile follows her around, and hijacks every later tap
cards.detail: BUILT AND DEPLOYED 29 July 2026, manager run 8, commit d6f99c6, CI green. THIS CARD WAS RAISED AS PB-048 AND RE-NUMBERED TO PB-050 - not by choice. The workbench UI saves joe/backlog.json whole, and Joe's page was open on a copy loaded before the live-bug card was committed, so two successive saves dealt his own new cards the id PB-048 and overwrote this one. His cards keep the ids he gave them; this one moved. docs/MANAGER-ORDERS.md item 0 and commit d6f99c6 both still say PB-048, and that is the same work as this card. LIVE BUG, reported by Joe from Juno playing the deployed build: "if a tile has been started and then abandoned, then tapping any tile jumps back into the building of the same tile, frustrating for her if she tries to tap an animal." THE RULING WAS JOE'S AND SETTLED: "if she abandons a tile, the progress towards reward is saved, the location and type is not. so when she then taps another glowing tile to build one, progress picks up but location and type is rechosen by her on entry." HOW IT WAS BUILT: a standing plot while the flow is in free play IS the abandoned state, because the sum overlay stays open across every sum of a tile - so she is only ever back on the island mid-build by having left one. askForLand no longer resumes a standing plot, it always opens the bank (flow.ts:236-261). placeTile now RELOCATES a standing plot instead of refusing to site over one (flow.ts:599-623). A tile tap starts nothing and resumes nothing, ever (interactions.ts:225-241), which is what kills the animal near-miss, because picking answers with whatever is under the ray and a missed tap at a pet is the tile beneath it. THE ABANDONED SCAFFOLDING IS DELIBERATELY LEFT STANDING rather than removed: that is what stops flow.plot ever transiently going null, and had it gone null the plot host would have played the completion farewell (plot.ts:111-133), so an abandoned tile would have looked like a finished one. Tests drive the real createPlotHost and the real handleWorldTap together at tests/island/plot.test.ts:402-534, watched failing first; seven existing tests across interactions.test.ts and flow.test.ts asserted the resumption and were rewritten rather than deleted, two of which had been passing vacuously off fixtures that never had a plot at all. cards.title: A ring of six mountain hexes seals a pet in for good
cards.detail: MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. PB-036 phase 3 spotted that scenery placement checks overlap with `footprintOf` (an axis-aligned half-extent, measured PRE-ROTATION) while pets collide against `blocks`, which uses `footprintBelow`'s rotation-invariant reach — two disagreeing metrics on the same object, at src/island/world/props.ts:1214 vs :1271. Phase 4 measured whether that can actually trap a pet on an island a child plays. IT CAN, and the reproduction runs the REAL placement code against the REAL mountain_*.gltf assets, not a mock. THE REPRO: grass at (0,0), rock at all six neighbours. All six mountains place; none is refused. Adjacent hex centres are 2.0000 exactly (hex depth 2.3094 -> hexSize 1.1547 -> sqrt(3) x 1.1547). Every consecutive pair of keep-out circles OVERLAPS, by -0.0657 to -0.1249. Flooding the plane at 1cm under exactly clearOf's constraint (pets.ts:382 — a pet centre is legal iff hypot(pos - ob) >= ob.r + self) shows a pet of radius 0.000 CANNOT LEAVE: reachable area 3.607 sq units, escapes=false. At the real field radius 0.186 it is 2.201 sq units and still sealed. The six circles form a closed annulus. CORRECTED NUMBERS. `footprintOf` is 0.9381 for the A/B mountain family but 1.0115 for the C family — phase 3's single figure of 0.938 was the A/B one. `footprintBelow` worst case is 1.0625 (mountain_A_grass_trees); the A/B family is 1.0388 and the C family 1.0269. Rotation-invariance of `footprintBelow` is CONFIRMED: identical at all six spins for every model, by hexagonal symmetry. Phase 3's line numbers are right but the file is src/island/world/props.ts, not src/island/props.ts. WHY THE EXISTING GUARANTEE DOES NOT COVER IT, which is the part that matters. docs/HANDOFF.md:453-464 records that "she cannot wall herself in" is delivered by `coast.hasOutwardCorridor` — a dry chain from her fields to open sea, inductive from Fred's rock rather than measured. That corridor walks ONLY `dryEmpty` cells (coast.ts:1056-1058: `tileAt(island, a) === undefined`), so it never sees a placed tile, a scenery footprint or a pet. It is about where SHE CAN STILL BUILD, not where A PET CAN WALK. Worse, rock is explicitly exempted from it at flow.ts:511-524 on the grounds that "rock is dry land and cannot have water beside it ... and can never cut a corridor" — true for building, FALSE for walking. That asymmetry is the whole hole. NO RECOVERY ON THE PET SIDE. There is no pathfinder and that is deliberate (pets.ts:794-795). `clearOf` (pets.ts:369-413) is a hard positional clamp, not a push, so it cannot move a pet through the ring. Stuck handling (pets.ts:830-837) rerolls the GOAL after 1.2s, never the position, and `randomSpot` (pets.ts:607-626) samples any owned tile uniformly, so on an N-tile island roughly (N-1)/N of goals are unreachable. Net: the pet lives forever in a disc of radius ~0.6, mostly pressed into a rock face, re-rolling every 1.2s. Not crashy — it reads as "that bunny never goes anywhere" — but PERMANENT, and it survives save/reload because the geometry is deterministic from the hash. REACHABLE IN PLAY. Rock unlocks at 15 placed tiles (balance.json, gated at flow.ts:417-421). `canBeRock` (coast.ts:503-505) forbids only water adjacency, so on dry ground all six sockets accept rock and all six glow. The cost is one tip hex plus six rock taps. A child who likes mountains around her bunny does it by accident. The pet must be on the tile when the sixth mountain lands, so it is roughly pets/tiles per closure — not certain per attempt, not rare, permanent once it happens. EVERY OTHER CANDIDATE IS CLOSED. Mountain hexes ARE impassable by design (governors.ts:198-217, "there is nowhere on it for a pet to stand") — but the SEALED TILE IS GRASS, which pets walk. There is no independent minimum-spacing rule: `firstClear`/`standsInside` (props.ts:426-458) is the only one, and for rock `spread = 0` gives a single candidate. Placement does not forbid adjacent mountains; 6 of 6 placed. THE FIX IS NOT A CONSTANT, and HANDOFF.md:464 says so in as many words: "if you are tempted to fix a sealing bug by moving a constant, the constant is not the problem." Swapping `footprintOf` for `footprintBelow` at props.ts:1214 makes it WORSE — it refuses every adjacent mountain pair and turns ranges into bare rock hexes. The two metrics are each right for their own question. The disease is that A MOUNTAIN HEX IS TERRAIN MASQUERADING AS A PROP: it is placed through the prop path (spread, firstClear, one collision circle) while governors.ts:201 already states it IS the tile. So the fix is to model rock hexes as impassable CELLS in a walkability layer, stop consulting `footprintBelow` for them, and add a pet-side corridor check at flow.ts:524 parallel to `corridorAfter` — refusing the KIND and falling back to grass exactly as line 524 already does for `canBeRock`, so she never loses a tap. That is a second invariant of the same species as the existing one, proved inductively rather than measured. NOT ATTEMPTED IN THE PB-036 PHASE 4 RUN, deliberately. The orders were to fix it this run if it genuinely traps pets, and it does — but the measured fix is a topological invariant across src/island/world/ and flow.ts, guarded by parity, in a subsystem a species run holds no context on. Shipping a half-understood walkability layer to close a sealing bug is how the FIRST sealing bug was shipped. It wants its own manager run, and it outranks more animals. The child-facing half (a rock tap that silently becomes grass) is Joe's call and is raised separately.
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug, and built MUCH smaller than the card above proposes — read the ruling before the analysis. Joe answered JT-033 with 'C - just relocate the animal from a trapped position, that is no issue at all', so this shipped as RECOVERY, not prevention: no walkability layer, no pet-side corridor check, no rock tap that silently becomes grass, and she never loses a tap. `walk.ts: rescueHexFor` names a destination and `pets.ts` moves the pet from two call sites. It is stateless and runs off the load path, so an island that ALREADY sealed a pet repairs itself the next time she opens it — no migration. Verified by a revert probe: exactly the 4 recovery assertions fail without the fix, the 8 negative ones stay green. The long analysis above is kept because its measurements are sound and were what justified the ruling; its PROPOSED FIX is now historical and must not be built. One thing deliberately NOT built: `firstFreeSpot` still hatches a pet without a reachability check. Recovery covers it, so prevention there is only wanted if Joe wants it — where an animal appears is his call.

cards.title: One rock hex in seven has no mountain on it, permanently
cards.detail: FOUND WHILE MEASURING THE SEALING DEFECT ABOVE, same root cause, and far more frequent — this one is almost certainly already visible in play and nobody has filed it. Placement tests overlap with `footprintOf` at src/island/world/props.ts:1214. For the C mountain family (mountain_C, mountain_C_grass, mountain_C_grass_trees) `footprintOf` measures 1.0115, so two adjacent C-family rock hexes give 2 x 1.0115 = 2.0230 against an adjacent-centre spacing of exactly 2.0000. `standsInside` therefore fires. Because rock uses `spread = 0` (props.ts:1179), `firstClear` has a single candidate and all six tries are the same point, so it returns null — and props.ts:1232 does `placed.add(k); continue`. THE SECOND MOUNTAIN IS NEVER PLACED AND NEVER RETRIED. A rock hex with nothing on it, for the life of the save. MEASURED OVER 19,440 ADJACENT PAIRS against the real hash: 14.5% of adjacent rock-hex pairs. The A/B family measures 0.9381 and stays under the bar, which is why it is one family in three rather than all of them, and why it looks random rather than systematic. DO NOT FIX BY MOVING THE CONSTANT. Raising or lowering the bar trades this bug against the sealing bug in the card above — tightening to `footprintBelow` (1.0269-1.0625) refuses EVERY adjacent pair and generalises this defect to 100%. Both cards are the same underlying fault: a mountain hex is terrain being placed through the prop path. Fix them together, or fix this one only by giving a refused rock hex a retry that can actually succeed (a smaller family member) rather than by widening the tolerance.
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug, alongside PB-052. Fixed the way the card said it should be — a refused mountain gets a SECOND TRY with a narrower peak (`mountainFallbackFor`), chosen from the measured footprint table rather than a name list, so it stays true if the models change. The constant was not moved and the primary chooser was not touched, which is what keeps existing islands rendering identically: 2763 refusals before, 2763 refusals after, 0 bare hexes remaining. `keepOutFor` now returns the max of primary and fallback, deliberately conservative because it cannot see neighbours.

cards.title: pettap.test.ts flakes about one run in six, and it is not species work
cards.detail: PRE-EXISTING AND PROVED AGAINST THE COMMITTED TREE, which is the fact that matters: PB-036 phase 3 dispatched an agent to run it against the tree WITHOUT that phase's species work applied, and got 2 failures in 12 cold runs — roughly 1 in 6, under cold-cache load. So it is not from the species layer and no species run should be blamed for it or should silence it. The test is `tests/island/pettap.test.ts:508 > does NOT let the camera into the keep-out or the blob`. MECHANISM. src/island/pets.ts seeds a pet's `phase` and `restFor` from `Math.random()` (pets.ts:695, :697) and the pet resets to (0,0,0) — exactly the obstacle centre, where push-out is degenerate, because `clearOf` (pets.ts:369-413) is a positional clamp and at zero separation there is no direction to clamp along. Under load the timing lets the assertion sample that degenerate instant. `tests/island/governors.test.ts > leaves a wide corridor...` shows the same load sensitivity from the same cause. THE HONEST FIX IS A SEED, NOT A RETRY. The randomness is real and is in the product; the test asserting on it without controlling it is the defect. Inject the rng the way the rest of this repo does rather than adding a retry loop or a tolerance, both of which would hide a genuine degenerate case at the obstacle centre — and that degenerate case is worth understanding on its own, since it is the same "pressed into a rock face" geometry as the sealing card above. NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS IT UP: two comments in the tests still narrate the old plot resumption as current behaviour (pettap.test.ts:13 and retype.test.ts:193). It is impossible since PB-050. They are historical narration, left deliberately, and are not documentation of what the code does today.
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug, fixed the way the card demanded — `createPetField(base, rng = defaultRng)` threads the repo's Rng through all five Math.random() sites in pets.ts and the test seeds it. No retry, no tolerance, nothing silenced. BUT THE CARD'S DIAGNOSIS WAS HALF WRONG and the correction matters more than the fix: it is NOT load-sensitive. The one-hex test island makes ~12% of opening goals land inside the 0.12 arrived radius, setSObstacles zeroes restFor, frame one re-plans — and the test reset only the pet's POSITION, when goal and restFor are pet state too. Also disproved: governors.test.ts does NOT share the cause, it contains no randomness at all (14/14 green, untouched) — so the card's claim that it shows 'the same load sensitivity from the same cause' was wrong and nobody should chase it. EVIDENCE: 1 failure in 14 cold runs before, 0 in 16 after, three of those taken while the full 2,739-test suite ran concurrently. SEED=11 reproduces the original failure deterministically, which is what proves the assertion still has teeth rather than having been defanged.

cards.title: JPGs in album often have a load lag
cards.detail: when opening the animals in the album there can be a load lag. explore idea of copying the already loaded 3d models? check computational demand
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug, and the premise was wrong in Joe's favour: THERE ARE NO JPGs AND NEVER WERE. Album portraits have always been rendered from the models, so 'copying the already loaded 3d models' was not an idea to evaluate — it was already the design. What was actually costing the lag: the album kept its OWN private GLTFLoader and re-fetched up to 24 GLBs / 3.26 MB that the island already had in memory, in copies that were also missing the face-decal fix. It now takes `pets.preview`, the cache holds the in-flight promise so a fast page turn cannot start a second fetch, and turning a page warms the next one on idle. No new render path was built — the thumbnail pipeline and the offscreen render-to-texture were costed and rejected in the header comment, so the next reader does not re-open the question.

cards.title: Gender in the game
cards.detail: Make it gender agnostic - users (children) should be referred to as "they". Fred stays male, other animals have no gender, teacher has a female voice but otherwise their gender is irrelevant. the owl later shall be female, if we ever use her DONE 2 Aug 2026. Only SIX gendered strings were ever visible to a human, all in the grown-ups panel, none child-facing. The spoken script needed nothing at all — the splice law had already got there — proved by diffing all 17 spoken text fields and finding them byte-identical, so this card was never blocked on the Azure key despite looking like it was. The real defect was prose: 1,621 gendered lines across 123 files down to 52 across 18, every survivor deliberate (34 are verbatim Joe quotations, left exactly as he said them). The deliverable is tests/copy/pronouns.test.ts, which scans every string literal in src/ and immediately earned its keep: PB-047 had shipped TWELVE new gendered strings into the wipe screen while this branch was being written, and the guard went red naming each one. SCOPE CLARIFIED by Joe 2 Aug 2026, and it is two-tier: "children are referred to as they in the parent set up, but only you in the game as it talks to them. both are gender agnostic." So the grown-ups panel talks ABOUT the child to an adult and uses they; the game talks TO the child and uses you, never they. Verified against the shipped tree: every they/them in child-facing copy refers to eggs, animals or questions, never the child, and the child is addressed as you throughout. Nothing needed changing — the second person was already right. The rule is recorded in the header of tests/copy/pronouns.test.ts because it cannot be mechanically enforced: distinguishing a they that means the child from a they that means the eggs needs to know what the sentence is about.

cards.title: new game types
cards.detail: Brainstorm and implement new game types to break up the monotonous pure maths approach

cards.title: The album opens collections that have no animals built
cards.detail: The four albums are drawn at random and the draw does not know which collections have models. Only base, garden, home-pets, woodland, africa and farm can be drawn; the other 15 show as rows of empty frames. Fix is one line: put the unbuilt ids in HELD_BACK (species/unlock.ts), which is already a holding pen meant to shrink. Second question in the same place, Joe's call: should the four Red List tiers be drawn for a five-year-old at all?
cards.note: DONE 1 Aug. The 'one line' was half the fix, and the missing half was the one that mattered. HELD_BACK gates the DRAW only, so a save that had ALREADY drawn an empty collection kept it forever: `completion()` divides by roster size, an unbuilt collection can never reach complete, never goes inactive, and so wedges one of the four active slots permanently. `advance()` now prunes a held-back collection, but ONLY when she owns nothing from it — §19 by construction, and the owning case is tested with real data. The held-back set is now the union of Joe's three and twelve with zero models, DERIVED from `shippedIn()` rather than transcribed, with a tripwire test that goes red naming the collection the day one ships. Starvation and deadlock were checked: the pool degrades to fewer open albums and never loops. The card's list of six buildable collections was not trusted and turned out to be stale.

cards.title: A new album opens silently
cards.detail: She finds it next time she taps the book. No moment was asked for so none was built. Does it want one?

cards.title: A task can be ticked done while its own check is red — voicesCast has never run
cards.detail: JT-003 was marked done with all three voices still cast:false, and joe/voices.json kept placeholder Ryan/Sonia while Joe's actual casting (oliver/olivia/thomas) sat only in the task's note field. Cause: checks.mjs:16 early-returns {ok:true} for any doneRule that is not 'artefact', and JT-003 is 'manual'. JT-003 is voicesCast's ONLY user, so that validator has never executed once. Proved by running it both ways against the old file: as declared it returns ok:true; as 'artefact' it returns 'still on placeholder voices: fred, teacher, owl'. Two ways out and it is a design call: flip JT-003 to 'artefact', or let checkTask run validators for manual tasks in warn-only mode, which matches the file's stated design that the Done button warns and never refuses. voices.json is already corrected; this card is about the hole, not the data. Second hole, found separately and worth fixing at the same time: even if voicesCast did run, it only tests the cast boolean — it never compares joe/voices.json against the ruling written in the task note, which is where the oliver/olivia/thomas casting actually lived. A check that asks "did someone tick a box" cannot catch "the box was ticked and the file was never written".

cards.title: Fred’s mouth and the hatch ceremony still guess at timings that are now known
cards.detail: Fred’s jaw-flap is driven by text length (main.ts:1757, main.ts:1584) and the hatch ceremony’s follow-ups are wall-clock, both because nothing knew how long a line actually lasted. The manifest now carries a measured ms for every clip, read from the Opus granule rather than estimated, so both could be driven by real duration. For the 6 lines still on speechSynthesis there is no duration to read, so whatever replaces the guess has to keep the guess as its fallback rather than assume a clip exists.

cards.title: The editor becomes the tool: add/swap parts, exact placement, refloor, sign-off, one-button push to the game
cards.detail: Joe, 2 Aug: "the editor is currently a good start, but its far off what i need it to be." Seven pieces, and he wants them in SMALL STEPS with check-ins, not an autonomous build loop. (1) Add components to an animal or swap them out. (2) Exact placement — "i cannot easily move any object to exactly where i want it, some of them snap even with snap off", which is the phase-7 snap bug not fully dead. (3) Move the legs UP, and the model then REFLOORS to that new height. (4) Base shapes: triangle, circle, square, same chamfer as the game, resizable (JT-041 — primitives only). (5) Parts library sorted with headers, by ROLE (JT-038). (6) Sign off the name and the fact line in the editor. (7) One button that pushes the finished animal into the game — today Save only writes a draft to joe/species-edits.json and never touches a shipped species, so promotion does not exist yet and that is the real destination. SHIPPED 2 Aug 2026, six of the seven pieces. Exact placement (legs take a y and the model refloors; ridge rows are hand-placeable per row over the solve), the dropdown grouped by role, and the three chamfered primitives with a resize that RE-CUTS rather than scaling baked positions. Add and swap already worked — what made them feel broken was the placement. Sign-off fills the four fields the draft always carried; the push writes six of the nine places and names the other three by path. Left: the three test files and the two shared counts stay a human’s, deliberately.

cards.title: building-animals-from-parts.md is wrong about box-03’s chamfer, and every species build reads it
cards.detail: §791 says box-03 "cuts every edge AND every corner". The points it lists are right; the topology is not. Measured off bank.generated.ts while building the primitives: 30 faces are 6 flat plus 24 bevel quads, TWO per edge at 56.31 degrees rather than one at 45, and there are ZERO corner facets — the eight (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) points are vertices where six quads meet. The cause is a grid snap: three exact 45-degree planes meet at 0.46875, which is 7.5/16 and off the pack’s own 1/16 grid, so Kenney rounded to 0.5. The doc should be corrected in place, because it is the file every future species build is told to read.

cards.title: The parts bank is generated at a precision that makes two eye cards unwearable
cards.detail: bank.generated.ts stores size to 6dp and positions to 4dp. The drift is enough to fail assembly-assert §3, which compares built size against part.size at 5e-5: plate-14/15 drifts 7.2e-5 and plate-06/07 drifts 5.8e-5. Every eye card that passes today is exactly 0.400 wide, which is why nobody hit it sooner. The fix is regenerating at finer position precision in tools/pets/parts-bank.ts — NOT weakening the assertion, which is the one rule a fit-to-height would break without a bounding box noticing.

cards.title: Three exhaustive tests fail only when the suite competes with a build for CPU
cards.detail: coast "never walls their island in", sealing, and facedecals each pass alone in seconds and time out during a full run with an agent building in parallel. They failed and re-ran green four times on 2 Aug. Measured: the coast test is 8.8s alone against a 30s budget. The suite has grown 128 to 152 files in a day, so this will get worse. Two honest options — cap vitest’s worker count so the suite stops starving its own slowest test, or give the three a real budget with the measurement recorded. Widening a budget silently to absorb load is the thing to avoid.

cards.title: One broken audio path silences the whole game, with no error and nothing on screen
cards.detail: Every sound the game makes goes through Web Audio — the voice player, the baked clips and the sound effects all build an AudioContext, and nothing in src/ uses an <audio> element. Found 2 Aug when Joe got total silence on his laptop while YouTube played fine: media elements and Web Audio are different output paths in Chrome, and only the media one worked. The game is fine (confirmed on the tablet, synth and baked both working), but a child in the same state would get a silent game with no error, no fallback and no indication anything is wrong — the ceremonies would still run, because speech.ts backstops onend at 2500ms whatever happens. Worth deciding whether the game should notice its own silence: an AudioContext that never leaves suspended, or a decode that yields no audible output, is detectable.

cards.title: Sign-off needs the animal moving on hex tiles, not standing on a turntable
cards.detail: Joe, 2 Aug: "i need to see the animals in the game environment, so in the editor i need to see it on like 7 hex tiles bouncing around like it would in the game. the it gets signed off." So this GATES sign-off rather than following it — he judges an animal moving, at distance, on ground, not still on a grey stage. The behaviour already exists in pets.ts (goal, restFor, bounce, and the hover for flyers) and the editor stage is tools/workbench/public/editor/stage.ts. Bring the island’s own wander loop to the editor rather than writing a second one; a second one drifts, and then he is signing off a thing that does not exist. MEASURED THIS RUN, and it makes this card bigger than it reads: no hand-assembled animal can be a live pet at all today. pets.ts builds a pet only from pets/<id>.glb, so an assembled species 404s and sync() silently drops it (pets.ts:777); dealing draws only from the 24 Kenney ids (main.ts:481). So the wander loop cannot yet show ANY of the 30 animals awaiting sign-off, and the preview must not be faked around that — giving pets.ts an assembly path is the first half of this card. AMENDED 2 Aug: the first half is done under PB-070 — pets.ts has an assembly path, so the wander loop can now show all thirty. What is left of this card is the editor preview itself, and its one real problem is unchanged: the editor shows an UNSAVED draft, so prototype()'s id lookup will not find the draft geometry.

cards.title: Whether an animal flies is a hardcoded set of two ids, and it should be Joe’s field
cards.detail: Joe: "editor also needs to let me decide if it flys or bounces on land." Today it is FLYERS at pets.ts:51 — a Set holding animal-bee and animal-parrot. Its own comment argues it must be a LIST and not a rule, because a rule saying "has wings" would put a penguin in the canopy; that reasoning is exactly why it belongs to Joe rather than to a constant. Already biting: no hand-assembled species can be marked flying at all, so Night Time’s nightjar cannot fly while the kiwi correctly should not, and nothing can express the difference. Design the field knowing water is coming (PB-069) rather than as a boolean to be widened later.

cards.title: Confine sea creatures to water, and keep land animals out of it
cards.detail: Joe, 2 Aug, explicitly LATER: "later we will confine sea creatures to water tiles only and stop land animals from going into the water." Both directions, not one. Belongs with habitats (PB-017) and the biome ladder (PB-022), and it should read the same per-species field that PB-068 creates rather than a second one beside it. NOTE ON IDS: commit 58f3ef7 says fix(PB-069) and is not this card — it is the flat-card standoff, PB-071.

cards.title: A signed-off animal still cannot be dealt, so sign-off alone does not put it in the game
cards.detail: Dealing draws from SPECIES, the 24 Kenney GLB ids (main.ts:481), never from the 54-record registry — measured, and no test asserts the two pools agree. So even once Joe signs off the 30 hand-assembled animals they can never reach a child. The standing order says a signed-off animal ships with the next push, always, and today that order cannot be honoured. Needs the assembly path from PB-067 first, then the deal pool widened to signed-off species only. DONE 2 Aug: pets.ts prototype() now builds an assembled species from parts instead of fetching a GLB, main.ts deals from dealPool(SPECIES) = the pack plus every registered species Joe has signed off, and src/ reads that from a generated mirror (src/island/species/signed-off.json) the workbench regenerates on his tick, so no step stands between signing off and shipping. sync() no longer swallows a failed build. Proved end to end by tests/island/deal-assembled.test.ts: deal, hatch, render, walk, save, reload. NOTE ON IDS: commit 6d672e6 says fix(PB-070) and is not this card — it is the editor card drawer, PB-071.

cards.title: A flat card landed inside the face it joined, so no mouth could be seen
cards.detail: Joe asked for the smiley mouth and was right that we already had it — face-plate (flat cut-out sheet), 12 tris. It was never filtered out of the editor and the extras schema always expressed it; the donor transfer placed a zero-depth card exactly coplanar with the hull front face, where it z-fought into invisibility. Fixed with CARD_STANDOFF = 0.01, a number recovered three ways (EYE_CARD_Z minus box-03 front, Kenney own decal sheet, and plate-03 recorded bank offset) rather than chosen. NOT the same fault as PB-064, which filters on role eye and has never seen a card. NOTE ON IDS: the commits call this PB-069 and PB-070, both of which were taken by another manager working in the same worktree at the same time.

cards.title: The colour panel could not give a newly added part a colour of its own
cards.detail: Joe: "i dont seem to be able to colour a mouth with the colour i want". The engine always supported it — palette is an open Record and the texture is generated at slots.length — but the panel could only repaint an existing slot or repoint a part at another existing one, and addPaletteSlot had zero callers in the UI. An inserted part arrives painted from the coat, so the only way to recolour it repainted the body. Now an "own colour" row appends a slot and repoints just that part; append-only, because insertion order IS the texture layout. NOTE ON IDS: the commit calls this PB-071.

cards.title: Home Pets: build the 14 unbuilt species by hand assembly
cards.detail: Ship 2, currently 2/16 — corn snake and goldfish exist, and both carry a non-uniform stretch Joe has flagged, so do not copy them as the standard; the Garden fourteen are the exemplars. To build: hamster, guinea pig, budgie, gerbil, pony, ferret, gecko, chinchilla, canary, cockatiel, terrapin, rat, lovebird, degu. JT-041 IS AMENDED (see JT-043): do not author new named parts, but DO improvise missing anatomy by sizing and rotating what the bank holds rather than stopping — Joe: "bit of clever sizing and rotation will get a lot done". His sign-off in the editor is the gate that catches a substitute reading badly. DONE 3 Aug 2026 — all 14 built, Home Pets is 16 of 16 and every member is hand-assembled. They ship UNSIGNED; Joe's editor pass is still to come, and JT-045 lists every improvised part in one place for him to judge at once. Shipping them also needed 14 rows in names-audit.json, 14 checked facts in species-facts.json and four registry counts, none of which was in the card.

cards.title: Farm: build all 16 species by hand assembly
cards.detail: Ship 5, currently 0/16 — all sixteen were kit-built and are deleted. To build: sheep, goat, horse, donkey, goose, turkey, llama, alpaca, rooster, ox, mule, chicken, guinea fowl, quail, water buffalo, pigeon. HOOVES ARE RULED ON — Joe: "just use a two tone leg for hooves". legs already take a paint, so a hooved species is legs: { paint: { base: "limb", patch: { below: "hoof", at: 0.25 } } } — Paint.patch needs no triangle edge to cut along, so no geometry is added. Three constraints: at is a fraction of the part own height and must sit on the 1/16 grid (0.125, 0.1875, 0.25); the patch applies to the BASE slot only, so do not combine it with byBand; spin a patched part and the boundary spins with it. This is a general tool, not a hoof workaround — it is also fur socks, pale paws, a bird feet against its legs, a dark-stockinged fawn. JT-041 as amended by JT-043 applies: improvise by sizing and rotation, never author a named part. The pony (PB-073) is the worked precedent for the hoof and derives the 1/16 grid point in full.

cards.title: A save's pet list is the one field read back without sanitising
cards.detail: Measured under PB-070: fromSave does `Array.isArray(save.pets) ? save.pets : []` and trusts every record inside, while readPlot, readOnceFlags, readOpened and readAttainment all sanitise what they read. It was harmless while a species could only be one of 24 known ids; now that the deal pool grows with sign-off, a stale or hand-edited save can carry a species nothing can build. pets.ts now says so loudly rather than silently, which is the safety net — but the read is still the asymmetry.

cards.title: Push it to the game wrote nothing, and said it worked
cards.detail: Joe edited the hedgehog, pressed Push, and was told in green that it was in the game; nothing reached src/. push.mjs refuses to write a species module that already exists, and all thirty assembled species already exist, so the only file any push ever wrote was the MOVES table — and the client judged success by the absence of an error key rather than by whether the species file was written, so a 200 whose own say field read "Nothing was written" printed as success. Fixed three ways: an explicit replace intent on the request lets an edit SPLICE its definition block back into the existing file, preserving every byte outside it (the hedgehog carries 222 lines of argued prose above its definition, and regenerating the file would have eaten all of it); pushOutcome now calls any push that did not write place 1 a failure, in red, naming the file that did not change; and the emitter was itself lossy — nine of the thirty species lost authored precision to a 6dp rounder on a round trip, and CreatureDef.motion was silently dropped from DEF_KEYS. Round trip is now provably lossless 30/30, guarded by tests/tools/editor-round-trip.test.ts.

cards.title: The editor round-trips through EVALUATED values, so a push flattens expressions AND resolves solver flags
cards.detail:
THE CARD PREVIOUSLY NAMED THE WRONG FIX. It said the route was `def.ts:1313` — have defineCreature register the def beside the build. That is (a) already done, since 2b320ab, in creature.ts:947,961, and (b) incapable of helping: registration hands the editor a JavaScript OBJECT, and `sink: LEG_ROW.sink` was evaluated to 0.408163 by the engine before defineCreature was ever called. The loss happens at evaluation time, upstream of every register. A JS object cannot carry source text. The stale sentence has been corrected in place at tools/workbench/public/editor/def.ts.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST IS TEXT, and 84cd17a proved the damage is worse than constants. Three kinds, in ascending severity:
1. CONSTANTS FLATTENED. 14 species bind file-local constants to expressions; a push writes the decimal and strands the declaration. tsc catches this (TS6133) and PB-076’s staleBindings names the lines. Cost: a manual repair per push. Mitigated, visible.
2. PRECISION LOST. The editor round-trips at SIX DECIMAL PLACES. 1/1.335 pushes back as 0.749064, which is 3.3e-7 short. So the naive repair — put the identifier back — SILENTLY MOVES THE ANIMAL. Invisible to tsc and to review.
3. SOLVER FLAGS RESOLVED, and this is the one nobody had seen. The squirrel’s `chamfer: true` came back as a literal `at`, so the tail is now joined 0.1375 INSIDE the hull instead of on the chamfer. The slow-worm’s single 90-degree spin came back DUPLICATED as two, flipping the coil upright; it now measures 1.3312 against PACK_HEIGHT_MIN 1.43 and does not stand on the ground. The mole lost box-24 outright and sits at 389 verts against rule 9’s floor of 405. The dormouse lost box-23, its tail, replaced by an extra named after its own part id. NONE of this strands a binding, so tsc is silent and only the per-species suites caught it.

THE ROUTE, costed. Cheapest and recommended: send the def AS LOADED alongside the emitted module in the push payload, so push.mjs can restore an expression BY TEXT — if the number the editor loaded for key K equals the number it is now pushing, K was untouched, so put the old source text back verbatim. No arithmetic is evaluated, so it does not cross the line push.mjs may not cross, and it is conservative by construction: a key Joe really edited still flattens, correctly. ~150-250 lines across push.ts, push.mjs and the request type, plus a sibling to withRestoredConstants. Second route: parse the TypeScript in push.mjs and merge per key preserving RHS text — larger, and it puts a real parser in a file that has stayed regex-only on purpose. Third: carry provenance from source text into the editor’s model — largest, and it is the one that genuinely changes what an edit MEANS, which is the part reserved for you.

DO NOT widen withRestoredConstants to evaluate arithmetic. Its refusal is correct: push.mjs may not execute src/, and a wrong value moves an animal rather than leaving an unused import.

NOT STARTED. Route 1 changes the push wire format, which is the one path Joe is actively using to push animals, so it wants a run of its own rather than riding alongside a change to what a push writes.

cards.title: A pet's name came off an unfiltered coin toss, and one in 678 was obscene
cards.detail: Joe's six-year-old was dealt a rabbit called Defuck. The live hatch used petName(defaultRng) - unseeded Math.random - and src/core/names.ts's FORBIDDEN list carries shit, cock, dick, piss and arse but not fuck and not cunt, so 640 distinct obscene names were reachable at one hatch in 678. cards.title: LIVE: the shrew and the newt have a see-through hole in the front of the head
cards.detail: box-31 is an OPEN SHELL — 4 of its 77 edges are used by one triangle, forming a 1.000 x 1.000 aperture in the front face where the lion's blade-05 plate belongs. The material is THREE.FrontSide (assembly.ts:509-511 never sets side), so it is see-through to the sky, not a dark interior. In the album portrait (6.4 deg elevation, 32.4 deg yaw) 27.2% of the shrew and 30.9% of the newt is background. The frog is safe because it already wears blade-05; the terrapin was fixed the same way for 18 triangles. Both are SIGNED OFF, so the fix is Joe's call, not ours. No test can see this: assembly-assert reads bounding boxes, matches vertices to the bank (the hull IS a faithful box-31, hole and all) and counts triangles, and a missing face moves none of the three. cards.title: hulls.ts:189 says box-21 is "TALLER, and nothing else", and it is not
cards.detail: Measured off its own 340 points while building the budgie: below local y +0.4975 box-21 IS the 1.250 cube, world span identical to box-03's to four decimals, and everything above sits in two LUGS at |x| 0.218-0.454 with nothing on the midline. It is a cube wearing the FOX'S EARS — exactly the trap box-12 was for the badger. The follow-on claim that the lugs are therefore a CREST was tried on the cockatiel and REFUSED on four numbers: the lugs' only band is Kenney's 10-triangle inner-ear cut so they cannot be painted yellow on a grey bird; they leave 0.436 of bare crown (35% of the hull's width) where a crest is one midline plume; they stand 0.2550 proud, LESS than the 0.2754 of the cone-01 crest that replaced them, at 184 triangles against box-03's 60. cards.title: The round-trip guard times out under load, because its cost scales with the species count
cards.detail: tests/tools/editor-round-trip.test.ts round-trips EVERY registered species through emit, write and dynamic import. Home Pets took that set from 30 to 44 and it now exceeds vitest's default 5s under full-suite load, while passing alone in ~2s. Farm makes it 60. Deliberately not fixed by raising the timeout: the standing rule here is that moving a constant to make a gate green buries real faults. Wants a measurement and a decision — per-species cases, a longer budget justified by data, or the trip proved once and sampled thereafter.
